https://www.chronicle.lu/category/intern.text: Home News International News 2 Die as Firefighting Helicopters Collide in Greece, French Blaze Changes Course 2 Die as Firefighting Helicopters Collide in Greece, French Blaze Changes Course Published on Monday, 03 Aug 2026 08:59 by IK Share This Article: Rate this item: Firefighters battle wildfire near the village Agia Paraskevi, Greece, 2 August 2026; Credit: Reuters/Stelios Misinas AGIOS KONSTANTINOS, Greece (Reuters) - On Sunday 2 August 2026, two firefighting helicopters collided in Greece while helping to control a huge wildfire that had destroyed more than 100 homes northwest of Athens, while people fled another blaze on the tourist island of Kefalonia. Two people on one helicopter — a Greek and a Danish national — died, while the crew on the other, one person from Greece, one from the UK, survived, the fire service said. Investigations had started into what caused the collision, it added. Europe has been ravaged by wildfires this summer after a period of record-breaking heatwaves and little rain – conditions that scientists say have been exacerbated by climate change. Destructive blazes in France and Spain showed some signs of easing over the weekend, but several wildfires have broken out in Greece after a period of relative calm there. The two helicopters collided in the area of Psatha in the Attica region, Greece's fire service said in a statement. Video posted on the Forecast Weather Greece Facebook page appeared to show two helicopters closing to cross paths at low altitude, before the main rotor of the lower helicopter struck the underside of the other. The lower one then crashed in flames. The second helicopter then dumped its load of water and flew away. Reuters has not verified the authenticity of the footage. Investigations suggested the fire that started in the Greek region of Boeotia before spreading to Attica was caused by sparks from conductors on a private network transmitting electricity generated by wind turbines to the main power grid, the eKathimerini website reported. Two Greek nationals were arrested on suspicion of negligence, while another suspect remains at large, the report said. 'Force of nature' Gale-force winds that had fuelled a fire around Porto Germeno on the Gulf of Corinth 60 km northwest of Athens subsided, but flames crossed a mountain to the south and reached the settlement of Veniza and a military firing range, igniting unexploded ordnance. Emergency crews focused their efforts on preventing fire from advancing towards the coastal town of Megara, which has a population of around 30,000. "There are moments when the force of nature and the intensity of weather conditions exceed all human planning and every operational capability,” Prime Minister Kyriakos Mitsotakis said in his regular Sunday message. Greek authorities issued emergency alerts for evacuations for a number of settlements in western Attica, including an industrial estate near Megara. In the village of Agios Konstantinos, residents were doing their best to halt the spread of the blaze. "The fire has been burning since last night, it is certain that they cannot have forces everywhere. We as residents are doing everything we can,” said Tasos Tzempelikos, 61, who along with his son was pouring water on the fire. Overnight, several settlements on the Ionian island of Kefalonia were evacuated after a fire broke out in the Pastra area in the south. Fire in France changes course In France, a fire in the southwestern Var region switched direction after a change in the wind and surged into a forested area that was difficult to access, BFM TV reported. A new fire also broke out alongside a highway near the historic southern city of Carcassonne, apparently caused by a blazing vehicle, BFM TV added. Video on the channel showed huge plumes of billowing grey smoke and flames near the road. Authorities said they had closed the highway and evacuated a nearby animal park. In Montfort-sur-Argens in Var, Georges Blanc, who had fled the fire earlier, returned home and was busy putting out hot embers to prevent a flare-up, while firefighters watered the wider area. "With the combined efforts of the two Canadairs (firefighting planes) and the firefighters, I think you could say all the houses were saved ... And now, well, I'm coming back to check, because since I saw the flames, I thought the houses wouldn't have survived," he told Reuters. In central Spain, wildfires that ripped through tens of thousands of hectares over the past week were mostly under control, though firefighters were dealing with reignitions in some areas. In the western province of Caceres, a forest blaze erupted on Saturday 1 August 2026, prompting the evacuation of around 800 people. Those residents were allowed to return on Sunday but remained confined to their homes as the fire was still active. Hungary nuclear plant forced to shut Other European countries are struggling with drought and receding water levels in major rivers, including the Rhine and the Danube, which recorded its lowest-ever water levels in Hungary, Serbia and Romania. Hungary faces a critical five days, Prime Minister Peter Magyar said on Sunday, as the drying out of the Danube forced the country's sole nuclear power plant to shut for the first time in more than four decades, with a new heatwave looming. Falls in water levels amid a lack of rain have also disrupted shipping and tourism in Hungary and triggered water-use restrictions in more than 100 cities and villages. Danube levels in Serbia fell to their lowest since 1985, cutting the daily output of the country's biggest hydropower plant to only 20%, the energy minister said on Sunday. https://www.bbc.co.uk/news/articles/cvgy.text: Figure caption, Watch: Lava fountain and ash cloud as Indonesia volcano erupts By Toby Mann Published 6 September 2026, 06:12 BST Updated 10 minutes ago More than 150,000 passengers have been left stranded after a volcanic eruption forced Indonesian authorities to temporarily suspend operations at six airports. Jakarta's Soekarno-Hatta International Airport was the first to be closed on Sunday morning after ash from Anak Krakatau was detected in airspace near the airport. Transport minister Dudy Purwagandhi said so far 467 flights have been affected and asked airlines to consider diverting some flights to other airports. The volcano had started erupting late on Friday night, generating continuous seismic activity, lava fountains, and booming sounds across surrounding regions. Two more eruptions happened early on Sunday, authorities said. Image source, EPA Image caption, Anak Krakatau's latest eruption has cancelled flights and forced some schools to halt activities The transport ministry said the pause in operations mainly affected flights to and from Singapore, also other international routes including Doha, Sydney and Kuala Lumpur. Purwagandhi said the decision to temporarily close more airports was made after tests found that volcanic ash had spread towards West Java. He urged airlines to speed up processes for refunding tickets for passengers who have been affected by flight cancellations, and for airlines to provide timely information to those with upcoming flights to avoid overcrowding at airports. According to Indonesia's meteorological agency BMKG, ash reached as far as 20,000ft (6,000m) on Java on east of the volcano, and 50,000ft (15,000m) west of the volcano on the Sumatra side. Image source, Getty Images Image caption, Flights to and from Singapore - as well as Doha, Sydney, and Kuala Lumpur - have been disrupted Authorities have confirmed there is no tsunami warning linked to the recent activity of the volcano, which is in the Sunda Strait between the islands of Java and Sumatra. The health minister has urged residents in affected areas to stay indoors and wear face masks to protect against respiratory, eye, and skin risks. According to local newspaper Kompas, several schools cancelled activities on Saturday after students and residents reported eye irritations from the ash, while some fishermen had cancelled fishing trips at sea similarly reporting sore eyes. One resident, Aldi Candra Prayogi, told the outlet that he felt since Friday evening and it felt like "small grains of sand had gotten into my eyes", and that he needs to use eye drops to ease the irritation. The dust is so thick that he has to sweep the front yard of his house every five minutes, he also said. Anak Krakatau, which means Child of Krakatoa, has been sporadically active since it emerged from the sea at the beginning of last century in the caldera formed after the 1883 eruption of Mount Krakatoa. The volcano - also known as Anak Krakatoa - collapsed in December 2018, triggering a huge tsunami which killed over 400 people , and displaced and injured thousands more on the nearby coastlines of Sumatra and Java. Scientists found that some of the chunks of rock that slid from the volcano when it collapsed were about 70-90m high . The Pacific Ring of Fire refers to a string of volcanoes, earthquake sites and tectonic plates around the Pacific. It spreads across 40,000km (25,000 miles) from the southern tip of South America all the way to New Zealand. Roughly 90% of all earthquakes occur along the area and the ring is dotted with 75% of all active volcanoes on Earth, that's 452 individual active volcanoes. https://baltic-review.com/druskininkai-t.text: Share Tweet 0 Druskininkai’s Tourism Days combine the resort town’s lakes, forests, wellness facilities and cultural venues in a three-day autumn programme. Druskininkai is opening the autumn season with a programme designed to make the resort itself the main attraction. From September 25 to 27, the annual Tourism Days will bring together light art, food, spa experiences, exhibitions, guided tours and outdoor activities across the southern Lithuanian town. The event was announced by the Druskininkai municipal tourism service on September 23, two days before the programme begins. Its format reflects a broader travel trend: visitors are invited not simply to attend one headline performance, but to build a weekend around the town’s natural setting, wellness infrastructure, cultural institutions and local businesses. ([druskininkai.lt](https://druskininkai.lt/en/news/traditional-tourism-days-in-druskininkai-2026/?utm_source=openai)) A resort programme built around place The most distinctive evening feature will be “Stories of Water”, a sound-and-light installation staged beside Lake Druskonis on September 25 and 26. Rather than placing the event in a conventional indoor venue, the organisers are using the lakeside landscape as part of the experience, linking Druskininkai’s identity as a water and wellness resort with contemporary visual art. Another light-focused attraction, the “Bunker 3.0” installation exhibition, will run at the Tech Spa building from 4 p.m. to 10 p.m. on both evenings. The programme gives visitors a reason to move through the town after dark, while keeping the emphasis on architecture, atmosphere and public spaces rather than on a single enclosed festival site. ([renginiai.druskininkai.lt](https://renginiai.druskininkai.lt/en/event/4722/turizmo-dienos-2026?utm_source=openai)) Food, craft and local discovery During the day, a Tourism Days fair will operate from September 25 to 27 on V. Kudirkos Street, Taikos Street and near the Druskininkai City Museum. The official programme presents the fair as part of a wider food and taste route, with local producers and other participants helping visitors encounter the resort through regional products and culinary traditions. The Druskininkai Brewery is also offering tours and tastings throughout the weekend, with advance registration required. On September 26, the Velvetti bistro-restaurant will host a four-hand tasting dinner combining Japanese influences with Dzūkija culinary ideas as part of the town’s Japan Days programme. These activities give the weekend a distinctly local character. The fair and tastings are not separate from the destination story: they connect visitors with the town’s food businesses, creative producers and regional identity. ([renginiai.druskininkai.lt](https://renginiai.druskininkai.lt/en/event/4722/turizmo-dienos-2026?utm_source=openai)) Wellness remains central Druskininkai’s traditional spa offer is also being opened up through special activities and trial experiences. Participating hotels and wellness centres are offering selected pool, sauna and treatment opportunities, including limited free introductory visits at Hotel Violeta and Mineral Spa Draugystė. The programme includes a special offer at Mana Sleep & Spa, while the K. Dineika Health Park will host “Amber Sauna” sessions. The Druskininkai Water Park is planning sauna programmes led by sauna master Irmantas, with admission included in the regular water-park ticket. For travellers, the practical advantage is that the event can be approached at different levels. A visitor can spend the weekend in a traditional spa setting, combine wellness with cultural programming, or use the resort as a base for walking, museums and outdoor exploration. ([renginiai.druskininkai.lt](https://renginiai.druskininkai.lt/en/event/4722/turizmo-dienos-2026?utm_source=openai)) Art, poetry and guided routes The Tourism Days programme also highlights Druskininkai’s cultural history. The Druskininkai City Museum is presenting the exhibition “Jacques Lipchitz and Friends”, while the Jacques Lipchitz Museum is showing “Sculptures—Pilgrims”. The V. K. Jonynas Gallery will offer guided visits and educational activities connected with the work of the Lithuanian artist and designer. Poetry is included through events linked to the international “Poetic Autumn in Druskininkai” festival. A September 26 reading will invite participants to share a favourite poem by another writer and one of their own, while a separate children’s session will combine poetry with educational activities. Visitors can also join a guided tour focused on Mikalojus Konstantinas Čiurlionis and his connection with Druskininkai, explore the Snow Arena and the new Snow Hotel, or take a sightseeing train from the town’s harbour on September 27. A longer walking route will connect the village of Sūručiai with Ratnyčia, giving the programme a clear regional and nature-based dimension. ([renginiai.druskininkai.lt](https://renginiai.druskininkai.lt/en/event/4722/turizmo-dienos-2026?utm_source=openai)) A compact weekend destination The significance of the event lies in its combination of scale and accessibility. Druskininkai is not presenting Tourism Days as a one-off spectacle detached from everyday life. Instead, the programme uses existing streets, museums, parks, hotels, restaurants, galleries and attractions, allowing visitors to experience how the resort functions as a year-round destination. That approach is particularly suited to early autumn travel. The schedule encourages visitors to move between indoor and outdoor activities, with forest landscapes, lakeside installations, spa facilities, food events and cultural venues all within the same resort environment. For travellers looking for a short Lithuanian break between the summer and winter seasons, Druskininkai’s September 25–27 programme offers a concentrated introduction to the town’s main strengths: water, woods, wellness, food and culture. The full programme, including registration details and admission information, is available through the municipality’s event calendar. https://www.aljazeera.com/news/2026/10/2.text: Listen (4 mins) Save Share Romania says Russia-run sabotage network set fire near weapons factory on social media Share Add Al Jazeera on Google Exterior view of the Consulate General of the Russian Federation in Constanta, Romania [File: Costin Dinca/ Inquam Photos] By Al Jazeera Staff , AFP and Reuters Published On 27 Oct 2026 27 Oct 2026 Romanian authorities say they have uncovered a network “coordinated” by Russia that they believe was responsible for a fire at an industrial site near a state-owned weapons factory in September. Romania’s Intelligence Service said on Monday that the blaze in the central city of Brasov on September 14 was “part of a wider campaign of sabotage operations coordinated” by Russia amid its full-scale invasion of Ukraine. Recommended Stories list of 3 items list 1 of 3 Ukraine says Russian drone attack sinks ship in Romanian waters list 2 of 3 ‘Block, blunt, break’: What’s in NATO’s new Russia war plan? list 3 of 3 Seven missing after two tankers catch fire off Romania’s Black Sea coast end of list The agency said the operations were aimed at arms manufacturers and “other targets of military and industrial interest”. “These actions are intended to intimidate, undermine defence capabilities and weaken the contribution of the targeted states to European and regional security,” it said in a statement. There was no immediate comment from Russia on Romania’s claim. Moscow has previously repeatedly denied such accusations. Romania’s Directorate for Investigating Organized Crime and Terrorism, known as DIICOT, said three people had been involved in the Brasov fire – two Belarusians and a Ukrainian, all living in European Union countries. Two were “tracked down and remanded in custody in Germany while they were preparing to commit similar offenses”, the directorate said. The third remains at large in Poland. According to Romania’s Intelligence Service, recruits for such networks are often found on social media and are first offered money “for a seemingly harmless task”, such as “observing or photographing certain targets”. Over time, “the tasks become increasingly serious, potentially involving acts of vandalism, arson or even murder”, it said. Advertisement ‘Hybrid’ war Romania, a member of the EU and NATO, shares a border of more than 600km with Ukraine. Its centrist president, Nicusor Dan, has said the country is a target of a hybrid war that Russia is waging to destabilise nations backing Kyiv, citing drone incursions into Romanian airspace, cyberattacks, disinformation campaigns and sabotage. Foreign Minister Dan Neculaescu said the fire in Brasov was “part of a broader campaign of sabotage across Europe” targeting military production. “Hybrid attacks will not hold us back from strengthening our resilience and defense,” he wrote on X. The accusation follows a string of incidents at defence sites across Europe in recent weeks. In September, explosions and a fire erupted at an ammunition storage site in Bulgaria, weeks after a blaze at another munitions facility in the country. Both sites are operated by the Bulgarian arms maker EMCO, whose munitions are used in Ukraine. That same month, firebombs were thrown near the offices of a defence company in Munich, and Romanian authorities said they had detained a Russian citizen accused of filming and photographing military sites in preparation for sabotage. In August, a blast struck an ammunition factory near Rome in Italy operated by the arms maker KNDS. At sea, at least eight cargo ships have been hit off the coasts of Romania and Bulgaria over the past three weeks, and about 34 sailors have been reported dead or missing. Dan, the Romanian president, has called the attacks on ships in Romanian waters “a new example of the tragic consequences of Russia’s aggression against Ukraine”. A year ago, Poland and Romania also detained eight people suspected of taking part in a Russian plot to send exploding parcels to Ukraine.

https://www.politico.eu/article/burnham-.text: LONDON — Andy Burnham said Wednesday that the government will publish its 10-year plan before the U.K. parliament goes into recess for the Christmas break on Dec. 17. Speaking in the Commons, the prime minister told MPs: “I am determined to give this country the stability that they [the Conservatives] failed to provide, I am determined to give the leadership that this country needs.” He said ministers will "present our plan for Britain to this house before it rises for the Christmas recess.” Advertisement Advertisement Burnham's words follow speculation about the timing of the long-awaited document seen as pivotal to the government's agenda. The prime minister told the Economist last week there was no “firm landing zone” for its publication and “we may go into the new year, to be honest.” The Sunday Times reported the document will be divided into three sections — “growing up,” “getting on” and “growing old” — focused on the government's role throughout people's lives. Burnham told MPs the plan will come before the Commons next month and “lay a new path for this country, breaking with the failed policies of the party opposite.” He added that “it will lay a path for this country to go forward.” The prime minister said the plan will contain a “proposal for a national care service” and that cross-party talks on adult social care will take place “before the end of the year.”
